title: Sampling Conformational Ensembles of Highly Dynamic Proteins via Generative Deep Learning.
authors: Ruzmetov, Talant; Hung, Ta I; Jonnalagedda, Saisri Padmaja; Chen, Si-Han; Fasihianifard, Parisa; Guo, Zhefeng; Bhanu, Bir; Chang, Chia-En A
journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
one_liner_zh: 该文用生成式深度学习(ICoN)从MD数据中采样高度动态蛋白(含IDP Abeta42单体)的构象系综，虽未直接研究PPI，但为无序蛋白构象机制建模提供了可迁移的AI方法，对IDP介导互作的构象基础研究有重要启发。
abstract: Proteins are inherently dynamic, and their conformational ensembles play a crucial role in biological function. Large-scale motions may govern the protein structure-function relationship, and numerous transient but stable conformations of intrinsically disordered proteins (IDPs) can play a crucial role in biological function. Investigating conformational ensembles to understand regulations and disease-related aggregations of IDPs is challenging, both experimentally and computationally. In this paper, we first introduce a deep learning-based model, termed Internal Coordinate Net (ICoN), which learns the physical principles of conformational changes from molecular dynamics simulation data. Second, we selected data points through interpolation in the learned latent space to rapidly identify novel synthetic conformations with sophisticated and large-scale side chains and backbone arrangements. Third, with the highly dynamic amyloid-beta(1-42) (Abeta42) monomer, our deep learning model provided a comprehensive sampling of Abeta42's conformational landscape. Analysis of these synthetic conformations revealed conformational clusters that could be used to rationalize experimental findings. Additionally, the method can identify novel conformations with important interactions in atomistic details that are not included in the training data. New synthetic conformations showed distinct side chain rearrangements that are probed by our electron paramagnetic resonance and amino acid substitution studies. This approach is highly transferable and can be used for any available data for training. The work also demonstrated the ability of deep learning to utilize natural atomistic motions in protein conformation sampling.
abstract_zh: 蛋白质本质上是动态的，其构象集合在生物功能中扮演着关键角色。大规模运动可能主导蛋白质结构与功能的关系，而内在无序蛋白质（IDPs）的众多瞬时但稳定的构象在生物功能中可发挥重要作用。研究构象集合以理解IDPs的调控和疾病相关聚集，在实验和计算层面均具挑战性。本文中，我们首先引入一种基于深度学习的模型，称为内部坐标网络（ICoN），该模型从分子动力学模拟数据中学习构象变化的物理原理。其次，我们通过在学习的潜在空间中进行插值选择数据点，以快速识别具有复杂且大规模侧链和主链排列的新型合成构象。第三，针对高度动态的淀粉样β(1-42)（Abeta42）单体，我们的深度学习模型提供了对Abeta42构象景观的全面采样。对这些合成构象的分析揭示了可用于合理化实验发现的构象簇。此外，该方法能够识别训练数据中未包含的、具有原子细节重要相互作用的新型构象。新的合成构象显示出不同的侧链重排，这些重排通过我们的电子顺磁共振和氨基酸替换研究进行了探测。该方法具有高度可转移性，可用于任何可用的训练数据。这项工作还展示了深度学习在蛋白质构象采样中利用天然原子运动的能力。
